articles.title: Pharmacogenetics Governance for Youth Mental Health: A Scoping Review of Policy Across 13 Countries.
articles.abstract: Pharmacogenetics (PGx) testing could improve psychotropic prescribing for children and young people, yet youth-specific policy guidance remains scarce. This review characterizes the international PGx policy landscape for youth mental health across 13 countries. From 940 records, 20 policy documents met inclusion criteria, yielding 190 passages for thematic analysis using the GE3LS framework. We found that 75% of policies primarily focused on guiding medication prescribing in adult populations, with limited consideration of youth populations; only one (5%) was designed specifically for youth. Three-quarters of documents originated from professional organizations rather than governments, indicating a structural governance vacuum. An "inverted pyramid" of policy priorities was identified, with scientific (Genomics, 29.5%) and implementation (Social, 24.7%) considerations dominating over weak economic (7.9%) and legal (14.2%) foundations. Policy coverage primarily focused on medications used in adult populations (antidepressants 80%; cardiovascular 85%), with limited consideration of youth populations; anxiolytics, relevant in pediatric practice, were covered in only 5% of documents. Policymakers must prioritize enforceable, youth-centered legislation to address these governance failures.

Dual drug delivery via integrin-targeted nanoparticles enhances therapeutic efficiency in BRAFV600E colon cancer.
articles.abstract: Colorectal cancer (CRC) patients possessing the BRAFV600E mutation often fail to respond to current first line therapies and are associated with poor prognosis, despite the advent of orally delivered small molecule inhibitors (SMIs) targeting the RAS-RAF-MEK-ERK signaling pathway. Thus, further improvements are required at a formulation and delivery level in order to enhance survival of these patients. Here we have formulated nanoparticles (NPs) made from biodegradable pegylated poly(lactide-co-glycolide) (PEG-PLGA) polymers, co-loaded with the SMIs, encorafenib (a BRAFV600E inhibitor) and trametinib (a MEK1/2 inhibitor) and decorated with the integrin targeting moiety, cyclic arginine-glycine-aspartate (cRGD), that are capable of significantly enhancing therapeutic effectiveness upon intravenous (IV) delivery in a xenogeneic CRC model when compared to the soluble SMIs delivered IV at equivalent doses. Pharmacokinetic analyses revealed actively targeted NPs could deliver the SMIs more efficiently to the tumor than IV administered SMIs in soluble form while also reducing their accumulation in the skin, an off-target site often associated with the dose-limiting side-effects of trametinib. This work is the first to demonstrate the therapeutic benefit of targeted nano-based co-delivery of SMIs in BRAFV600E-CRC and warrants further progression toward clinical studies in order to improve CRC patient survival outcomes.

articles.title: Kinetically stabilized nanocondensates via guided co-assembly: resolving solubility-potency mismatches and solvent confounding in drug discovery.
articles.abstract: Physicochemical and vehicle-derived artifacts, such as precipitation and solvent-driven perturbations, often decouple nominal dose from the bioavailable aqueous fraction, leading to distorted potency and mechanism assignments in preclinical assays. Here we introduce e-PASS, a computationally guided co-assembly strategy that prioritizes pharmaceutically relevant excipients and generates kinetically stabilized, drug-rich nanocondensates. These nanocondensates act as dynamic reservoirs that sustain free-compound availability during assay-relevant dilution and handling, thereby improving dosing fidelity and maintaining aqueous exposure, as quantified by AUC-based metrics relative to conventional dimethyl sulfoxide dilution. Across chemically diverse kinase and antifibrotic inhibitors, e-PASS suppresses precipitation artifacts, mitigates dimethyl sulfoxide-driven confounding, and yields concentration-response relationships that more faithfully reflect intrinsic compound activity, with mechanism-consistent responses. Improved chemical availability further translates into enhanced systemic exposure and therapeutic efficacy in tumor and liver-fibrosis models. Together, these results establish nanocondensate reservoirs as a general physicochemical lever to overcome precipitation- and vehicle-derived artifacts and expand screenable chemical space for reliable discovery workflows.

articles.title: An mRNA-encoded Bispecific T-Cell Engager Targeting Muscle-Specific Tyrosine Kinase for Myasthenia Gravis.
articles.abstract: Muscle-specific tyrosine kinase antibody-positive myasthenia gravis (MuSK-MG) is a severe autoimmune disease with limited effective treatment options. We designed an mRNA-encoded bispecific T-cell engager (MuSK×CD3 TCE) comprising the human MuSK extracellular domain and an anti-CD3 single-chain variable fragment (scFv), delivered via a lipid nanoparticles (LNPs) to the liver to enable in vivo protein synthesis, which redirects cytotoxic T cells to eliminate B cells expressing anti-MuSK B cell receptors (BCR). In vitro, the MuSK×CD3 TCE mediated dose-dependent cytotoxicity against MuSK+ target cells and induced robust T cell activation. In human PBMC-engrafted NOG mice, mRNA-LNP administration led to dose-dependent and specific inhibition of tumor growth in anti-MuSK BCR-positive tumors, with no significant impact on non-target B cells. Importantly, the TCE retained potent cytotoxic activity in the presence of physiological concentrations of MuSK autoantibodies-a key consideration for clinical translation, as patients with MuSK-MG typically harbor circulating autoantibodies. This "off-the-shelf" mRNA-LNP platform offers a precise, controllable and potent immunotherapy strategy for MuSK-MG and may be broadly applicable for other autoantibody-mediated diseases to eliminate pathogenic BCR+ B cells.

articles.title: Title: Topoisomerase I Inhibition Serves as a Tumor Vaccine by Inducing the ERVs-dsRNA-Interferon Pathway.
articles.abstract: Double-stranded RNA (dsRNA) can activate potent anti-tumor immunity, but its clinical translation remains challenging. We sought to identify clinically applicable strategies to induce endogenous dsRNA and enhance anti-tumor immune responses. Here, we integrated genome-wide CRISPR-Cas9 screening data with the Therapeutic Target Database (TTD) and identified Topoisomerase I (TOP1) as a potential inducer of dsRNA. Mechanistically, we found that TOP1 was associated with suppression of endogenous retroviruses (ERVs) in an enzyme activity-dependent manner, and this was accompanied by "viral mimicry" through the induction of dsRNA. Pharmacological inhibition of TOP1 using Irinotecan (CPT-11) triggered dsRNA accumulation across cancer models, including patient-derived organoids (PDOs), activating the RIG-I/MDA5-MAVS pathway and antiviral interferon responses (Type I/III IFNs, ISGs). scRNA-seq revealed that CPT-11 remodeled the tumor microenvironment, promoting infiltration of dendritic cells (DCs), macrophages, and T cells. Combining CPT-11 with PD-1 blockade in "cold" tumors dramatically improved survival. CPT-11 also generated a potent in situ vaccine effect, establishing immunological memory that prevented tumor rechallenge. Moreover, tumor cells pretreated with CPT-11 in vitro were also able to exert a vaccine-like effect, inhibiting the growth of subsequently inoculated tumors. Collectively, our findings support the repurposing of TOP1 inhibitors such as CPT-11 to harness dsRNA-mediated immune activation for more effective cancer therapy.

articles.title: A novel α-glucan from Glehniae Radix protects against gastric ulcer and modulates complement-coagulation and NF-κB signaling.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Glehniae Radix is a traditional herb used to nourish yin (i.e., replenish body fluids and benefit the lung and stomach) and support gastric health. Although it is rich in polysaccharides, the contribution of these compounds to gastroprotection remains poorly understood. PURPOSE: This study aimed to evaluate the gastroprotective activity of Glehniae Radix polysaccharides (GLP), investigate the molecular pathways associated with its gastroprotective activity, and purify and structurally characterize homogeneous bioactive polysaccharide components contributing to this activity. STUDY DESIGN: The gastroprotective activity and associated molecular pathways of GLP were investigated using complementary in vivo and in vitro models. GLPE1-F was purified, structurally characterized, and evaluated for its biological activities and associated molecular pathways. METHODS: Pharmacological activities were assessed in an ethanol-induced rat gastric ulcer model, in GES-1 gastric mucosal cells, and in three zebrafish inflammation models (CuSO₄, LPS, tail amputation). Mechanisms were investigated using 4D-DIA proteomics, Western blotting, immunofluorescence, and time-course analysis. A homogeneous polysaccharide (GLPE1-F) was purified by anion-exchange and size-exclusion chromatography and characterized by HPGPC, HPLC, FT-IR, methylation analysis, and NMR. RESULTS: GLP significantly attenuated gastric mucosal hemorrhage and erosion in rats, preserved mucosal barrier integrity, and reduced inflammation and oxidative stress. In GES-1 cells, GLP enhanced cell proliferation while reducing apoptosis and ROS accumulation. GLP also mitigated inflammation in zebrafish models induced by CuSO₄, LPS, and tail amputation. 4D-DIA proteomics identified the complement-coagulation cascade and NF-κB signaling among the pathways affected by GLP treatment. GLP reduced the levels of complement-coagulation factors, including C1QA, MBL2, F12, F2, and C3, in RAW 264.7 macrophages, HepG2 hepatocytes, rat serum, and gastric tissue. NF-κB activation (IκBα/NF-κB phosphorylation and nuclear translocation) and the levels of TNF-α, IL-6, and IL-1β were also decreased following GLP treatment. GLPE1-F (Mw 6.986 kDa) was identified as a novel α-glucan with a backbone of →4)-α-D-Glcp-(1→ and C-6 branches consisting of α-D-Glcp-(1→ and α-D-Glcp-(1→6)-α-D-Glcp-(1→ units. GLPE1-F exhibited gastroprotective activity in rats, cytoprotective activity in GES-1 cells, and anti-inflammatory activity in zebrafish models, and modulated complement-coagulation and NF-κB signaling in rat and cellular experiments. CONCLUSIONS: This study identifies GLPE1-F as one of the bioactive components contributing to the gastroprotective activity of GLP and modulating the complement-coagulation cascade and NF-κB pathway, providing a scientific basis for its further development as a gastroprotective candidate.

articles.title: Salidroside regulates blood-brain barrier integrity via Lcn2-NLRP3 signaling axis inhibition for high-altitude hypoxic brain injury intervention.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: High-altitude hypoxic brain injury (HHBI) is a central nervous system injury disease induced by high-altitude hypobaric and hypoxic environment, which disrupts normal cerebral metabolism and neurological function and triggers multi-dimensional pathological damage in brain tissues. Among these pathological events, blood-brain barrier (BBB) injury represents a critical initiating and aggravating facet of HHBI, which drives subsequent cerebral inflammation, cerebral edema and progressive brain tissue deterioration. Current clinically commonly used drugs can only relieve partial discomforts caused by high-altitude hypoxia, and fail to achieve precise prevention and treatment of HHBI as well as favorable safety profile prognosis. Salidroside (Sal), the core active ingredient of the classic Tibetan medicine Rhodiola crenulata, exerts prominent anti-hypoxia and neuroprotective effects, yet its specific molecular regulatory mechanisms remain poorly elucidated. Combining in vivo and in vitro experiments, this study aimed to explore the novel mechanism by which Sal alleviates BBB injury and thereby prevents and treats HHBI via regulating the Lcn2-NLRP3 signaling axis. METHODS: After acclimatization, mice were randomly assigned to control, model, dexamethasone (0.5 mg/kg), and Sal (50 and 100 mg/kg) groups, followed by 7-day consecutive administration of corresponding drugs. A low-pressure oxygen chamber was used to simulate high-altitude environments to establish the mouse HHBI model. The WBP respiratory detection system and Morris water maze test were employed to assess alterations in respiratory function and memory cognitive capacity of HHBI mice. A hematology analyzer and H&E staining were utilized to characterize systemic and cerebral inflammatory injury, whereas evans blue staining and brain water content measurement were performed to evaluate hypoxic impacts on BBB permeability. Super-resolution imaging (NIR-Ⅱ imaging and TEM) was adopted to detect cerebral microvascular blood circulation and ultrastructural alterations. Subsequently, RNA-seq was conducted to screen potential molecular targets mediating Sal conferred therapeutic effects against HHBI. Moreover, molecular docking, DFT calculation, alanine scanning and LSPR analysis were implemented to simulate the binding potential and stability between Sal and proteins of the Lcn2-NLRP3 signaling axis, and protein-protein docking and Co-IP further verified the potential binding and regulatory interaction between Lcn2 and NLRP3. Western blot and multiplex immunofluorescence staining were used to demonstrate the molecular mechanism by which Sal alleviates hypoxic BBB injury via modulating the Lcn2-NLRP3 signaling axis. In vitro, a CoCl₂ induced hypoxic model was established in bEnd.3 cells. CCK-8 assay, EdU staining and LDH release assay were used to evaluate the effects of Sal on proliferative activity of hypoxic bEnd.3 cells. DCFH-DA and JC-1 staining were applied to detect intracellular ROS levels and mitochondrial membrane potential. Label-free cellular imaging enabled continuous monitoring of mitochondrial morphological changes under hypoxia, and TEM further observed mitochondrial ultrastructural damage. Mitochondrial superoxide, mPTP and mtDNA staining together with SOD, MDA, GSH-PX and ATP quantification were performed to analyze hypoxia and Sal mediated changes in mitochondrial function. Furthermore, cell scratch wound healing, tube-formation and cell migration assays examined hypoxic vascular functional changes, while TEER resistance and FITC-dextran permeability assays assessed paracellular permeability. Western blot combined with multiplex flow cytometry was used to analyze Sal regulated expression of Lcn2, NLRP3 and downstream inflammatory factors. In addition, the Lcn2 inhibitor ZINC00640089 and target specific siRNA were employed to validate the regulatory role of Lcn2 on NLRP3. Finally, CETSA was further performed to determine the binding stability of Sal to Lcn2-NLRP3 signaling axis proteins. RESULTS: The results demonstrated that Sal exerted robust anti-hypoxic neuroprotective effects in HHBI mice by alleviating cerebral hypoxic stress, suppressing neuroinflammation, improving cerebral microcirculation, maintaining BBB integrity, and upregulating TJ proteins. In vivo data indicated that Sal intervention markedly improved basal respiratory function and alleviated cerebral memory and cognitive impairment in HHBI mice. Meanwhile, Sal effectively mitigated cerebral inflammatory injury induced by acute hypoxic stimulation and restored excessive BBB hyperpermeability. Mechanistically, acute endothelial inflammation and TJ disruption serve as key drivers of HHBI progression, which is predominantly modulated by aberrant activation of the Lcn2-NLRP3 signaling axis. Combined molecular docking, DFT calculation, LSPR detection and alanine scanning analyses confirmed the high-affinity and stable binding of Sal to core proteins of the Lcn2-NLRP3 axis. Western blot and immunofluorescence staining further revealed that Sal effectively alleviated BBB damage by negatively regulating the Lcn2-NLRP3 signaling cascade, and verified the favorable colocalization of Lcn2 with cerebral vascular endothelium. In vitro experiments showed that Sal markedly reversed hypoxia-triggered mitochondrial dysfunction, as evidenced by reduced mitochondrial superoxide accumulation, inhibited mPTP opening and mtDNA leakage, as well as restored MMP, ATP synthesis, and balanced levels of SOD, MDA and GSH-PX, thereby suppressing apoptosis in hypoxic bEnd.3 cells. Furthermore, Sal stabilized endothelial vascular structure and barrier function, increased transepithelial electrical resistance and elevated TJ protein expression in hypoxic endothelial cells. Multiplex flow cytometry further validated the regulatory effect of Sal on hypoxic inflammatory responses. Moreover, intervention with the Lcn2 inhibitor ZINC00640089 and Lcn2-specific siRNA further confirmed that Lcn2 acts as an indispensable upstream regulator of NLRP3 inflammasome activation and subsequent inflammatory cascades. CONCLUSIONS: Collectively, this study demonstrated that Sal ameliorates acute hypoxia‑induced mitochondrial dysfunction, thereby inhibiting excessive Lcn2 accumulation, suppressing subsequent NLRP3 inflammasome assembly and activation, and blocking downstream inflammatory cascade amplification. These effects ultimately alleviate vascular structural and functional damage, thereby exerting prominent preventive and therapeutic effects against HHBI.

articles.title: CYP450 quantification and metabolic activation capacity of rat and hamster liver S9 fractions: implications for nitrosamine mutagenicity testing.
articles.abstract: N-nitrosamine impurities are a major concern in the pharmaceutical industry and public safety. The assessment of this chemically diverse group using conventional regulatory test batteries, including the Ames test (OECD TG 471), remains challenging. Consequently, refined strategies such as the Enhanced Ames Test (EAT) have been developed and recommended by regulatory authorities, requiring 30% induced rat and hamster S9. Recently, we showed that hamster S9 metabolizes short-chain N-nitrosamines more efficiently than rat S9, likely due to differences in the induction pattern of metabolizing enzymes. Metabolic activation by cytochrome P450 isoenzymes (CYP) is a critical step in the bioactivation of N-nitrosamines. Building on our previous publication, the present work focusses on key CYPs and sets the proteome data into perspective with in vitro mutagenicity data for selected N-nitrosamines. Targeted proteomics quantified CYP1A2, 2A6, 2C8/9/19, 2D6, 2E1, and 3A4 of rat and hamster orthologs in uninduced, Aroclor 1254-, and PB/NF-induced rat and hamster liver S9. In rat S9, induction markedly increased CYP1A2 and CYP3A1 (> 40-fold). For the selected set of CYPs, most protein levels in hamster S9 decreased or increased only slightly (< 6-fold) following induction, although baseline levels were higher than those in uninduced rat S9. Nevertheless, induced hamster S9 generated the strongest Ames responses for NDBA and 1-CPNP, indicating that induction enhances CYP activity beyond protein quantity alone. N-nitroso-atenolol was negative under all rat S9 conditions but positive in TA1535 only with induced hamster S9, indicating that larger NDSRIs require elevated metabolic activity for detection. These findings provide a mechanistic basis for species- and induction-specific differences in mutagenicity detection and contribute to a better understanding of the metabolic activation capacity of S9.

articles.title: Genomic Reassurance and Diagnostic Closure in Precision Oncology: A Preventable Hazard.
articles.abstract: Genomic findings can sharpen therapeutic decisions, but they can also provide false reassurance. In precision oncology, labels such as benign, nonactionable, or explanatory may be mistaken for evidence that symptoms or abnormal findings require no further evaluation. This Perspective argues that genotype-phenotype discordance should be treated as a safety signal. Simple report language, tumor-board checks, and artificial intelligence guardrails can preserve the value of genomics without allowing a molecular explanation to become diagnostic closure.

articles.title: Efficacy and safety of the cladribine, idarubicin, and cytarabine regimen for treating acute myeloid leukemia: a systematic review and single-arm meta-analysis.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVES: This research sought to provide exploratory evidence regarding the efficacy and safety of the cladribine, idarubicin, and cytarabine (CIA) regimen for acute myeloid leukemia (AML). EVIDENCE ACQUISITION: PubMed, Cochrane Library, Web of Science, and Embase databases were retrieved up to September 9, 2025. Meta-analysis was implemented utilizing R (version 4.5.1). RESULTS: All efficacy endpoints were analyzed and reported separately by disease status. In newly diagnosed (ND) AML, pooled estimates were: complete remission (CR), 72.7% (95% confidence interval [CI]: 66.4%-79.0%); complete remission with incomplete hematologic recovery (CRi), 7.1% (95% CI: 3.7%-10.6%); overall response rate (ORR), 80.4% (95% CI: 76.8%-84.0%); 1-year overall survival (OS), 60.5% (95% CI: 53.5%-67.5%); and 2-year OS, 65.5% (95% CI: 33.4%-97.5%). For relapsed/refractory (R/R) AML, only CR could be quantitatively pooled (pooled estimate 37.1%, 95% CI: 7.5%-66.6%), albeit with limited statistical power. CRi, ORR, and OS were not pooled owing to insufficient studies; available data are described narratively. The pooled safety estimates were: rash/skin reaction 34.3% (95% CI: 0.0%-85.0%), severe infection in ND AML 59.5% (25.2%-93.8%), severe bleeding in ND AML 5.9% (2.8%-9.0%), and 28-day all-cause mortality 6.1% (1.1%-11.2%). CONCLUSIONS: Results indicate promising remission in ND AML, particularly low- to intermediate-risk cases. In contrast, efficacy is limited in R/R AML. Severe infections remain a major safety concern. Given the small number of studies and single-arm pooling, findings should be interpreted with caution. Future research should prioritize larger well-defined R/R AML cohorts, standardized CIA dosing regimens, and head-to-head randomized controlled trials against contemporary standard-of-care regimens (e.g., 7 + 3 plus gemtuzumab ozogamicin, CPX-351, and venetoclax-based combinations). Further exploration of CIA combined with molecular targeted agents (e.g., FLT3/IDH inhibitors) and standardized reporting of long-term endpoints including event-free survival and relapse-free survival are warranted.

articles.title: Metal-Organic Frameworks (MOFs) for Targeted Drug Delivery: A Review of Design-to-Release Correlations.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Metal-organic frameworks (MOFs) are crystalline porous materials that consist of adjustable metal nodes and organic linkers. These properties enable MOFs to act as effective vehicles for drug delivery when designed to control the breakdown or opening of the framework upon receiving a trigger, such as a biological or chemical stimulus [1, 2, 3, 4]. Even though the latest advances in research into MOFs have expanded the literature, the published information on the correlation of the factors concerning the design of MOFs (the type of metal node and linker used, the size of the particles, and surface treatment) with the process of the release of drugs has not been conducted to the fullest extent. OBJECTIVE: This study aims to conduct a systematic review of the (i) synthesis and physico-chemical characterization methods applied to the development of stimuli-responsive MOFs used for targeted drug delivery and of the (ii) design-to-release relationships that govern the use of pH, redox, light, temperature, and enzymatic triggers. METHODS: The review follows PRISMA 2020 [5]. PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, and ScienceDirect were searched for English-language primary research published during 2014-2025. Two reviewers screened records and extracted information on MOF identity, synthesis, characterisation, loading, release and biological outcomes. Complete screening, extraction and appraisal records are unavailable for independent verification. The present synthesis is qualitative; selected numerical observations are attributed to individual studies, without pooled estimates or cross-study regression. pH-, redox-, light-, temperature- and enzyme-responsive systems illustrate the diversity of MOF-based delivery. ZIF-8, MIL-family, UiO-66 and porphyrinic carriers offer different loading and release strategies. Loading capacity, particle size and surface modification influence performance, but comparisons depend on cargo, formulation and assay conditions. The available documentation does not support a pooled release ratio, a BET-loading regression, or a universal size optimum. Animal studies were appraised with SYRCLE [6].

articles.title: Safety of proton pump inhibitors in children: A systematic review.
articles.abstract: AIM: To systematically evaluate the safety of proton pump inhibitor (PPI) therapy in children aged 0-12 years, with a focus on treatment-emergent adverse events across different study designs and age groups. METHOD: The systematic review was carried out according to the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) guidelines. Literature search was conducted across multiple electronic databases, including PubMed, Embase, Cochrane Library, Scopus, Google Scholar and Grey literature sources. Eligible studies included retrospective cohort studies, randomized controlled trials and phase 1/early-phase studies. Data extraction focused on reported adverse events, patient age, drug type and treatment duration. The methodological quality was assessed using study-design-specific tools. Randomized controlled trials were evaluated with the Cochrane Risk of Bias 2.0 (RoB 2) tool, observational cohort studies with the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale (NOS) and non-randomized interventional studies with the Methodological Index for Non-Randomized Studies (MINORS). CONCLUSION: Short-term PPI use in children appears generally safe, with predominantly mild gastrointestinal and respiratory adverse events. Serious complications are uncommon but may be underestimated due to limited follow-up and inconsistent reporting. Use of PPIs in infants with physiological reflux is discouraged, as gastric contents are typically non-acidic due to milk buffering.

articles.title: Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists in schizophrenia spectrum disorders: A systematic review and meta-analysis of efficacy, safety and mental health outcomes.
articles.abstract: AIMS: The purpose of this study is to evaluate efficacy, safety and mental-health outcomes of glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) receptor agonists in adults with overweight or obesity and antipsychotic-treated schizophrenia-spectrum disorders. METHODS: PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, PsycINFO, CENTRAL, Virtual Health Library (VHL) (Biblioteca Virtual em Saúde, BVS), Scopus, Web of Science and trial registries were searched on 28 August 2026. Random-effects models pooled mean difference (MD) or standardized mean difference (SMD) with 95% Wald intervals; Hartung-Knapp-Sidik-Jonkman (HKSJ) intervals were computed in parallel. Missing change-score SDs were imputed at r = 0.50 (sensitivity r = 0.25 and 0.75). Binary safety outcomes used Mantel-Haenszel risk ratios with a 0.5 continuity correction for zero cells. RESULTS: Six trials (n = 446) were pooled; three (n = 102) informed the primary outcome. The primary outcome of total symptom severity was imprecise (SMD - 0.21, 95% CI -0.60 to 0.19; HKSJ -1.02 to 0.61). Functioning, Alcohol Use Disorders Identification Test (AUDIT), Schizophrenia Quality of Life Scale (SQLS) and Brief Assessment of Cognition in Schizophrenia (BACS) were likewise imprecise; all intervals included the null. Secondary mental-health analyses were exploratory and unadjusted for multiplicity. Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1 RAs) reduced body weight (MD - 7.42 kg, -11.52 to -3.33; I2 = 94%), body mass index (BMI, -2.77 kg m-2), waist circumference (-5.53 cm) and HbA1c (-0.36%). Gastrointestinal events were more frequent; serious adverse events were not. Weight heterogeneity tracked agent, dose, duration and antipsychotic background. CONCLUSIONS: GLP-1 RAs were associated with improvements in cardiometabolic measures over 12-36 weeks, although certainty for body weight was limited by heterogeneity and risk of bias. Mental-health estimates were imprecise and did not allow a clear conclusion regarding benefit or harm. Cardiovascular events were not assessed, and no conclusions can be drawn regarding cardiovascular outcomes in this population.

articles.title: Targeting PLAGL2 in hepatocellular carcinoma and metabolic liver injury: molecular mechanisms and pharmacological opportunities.
articles.abstract: PLAGL2 is a C2H2 zinc-finger transcription factor increasingly recognized as a potential pharmacological target in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) and metabolic-inflammatory liver disease. Although PLAGL2 has traditionally been studied as an oncogenic regulator, recent evidence links it to therapeutically relevant adaptive programs in HCC, including the PLAGL2-EGFR-HIF-1/2α signaling loop, non-coding RNA-mediated PLAGL2/HIF-1α regulation, C-MET/STAT3-associated survival signaling, macrophage recruitment, extracellular matrix remodeling and resistance to targeted therapies. In parallel, hepatocyte-specific Plagl2 deficiency has been shown to alleviate metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH) by limiting MYD88-licensed inflammasome activation, pyroptotic signaling and IL-1β-associated macrophage activation. These findings suggest that PLAGL2 may operate at the interface of hepatocyte stress, inflammatory remodeling and tumor adaptation. Recent development of PLAGL2-directed small molecules, including compounds that suppress PLAGL2 transcriptional activity or target its DNA-binding domain, further raises the possibility that this transcription factor is pharmacologically approachable. This review critically evaluates PLAGL2 as an emerging therapeutic candidate in liver disease, focusing on hypoxia-linked signaling, inflammasome activation, extracellular matrix remodeling, therapeutic resistance and early pharmacological targeting strategies. We also discuss the attractive but still unproven hypothesis that PLAGL2 contributes to the MASH-HCC continuum.

articles.title: Restoring Myocardial Sodium-Calcium Homeostasis: A Central Mechanism of Empagliflozin in Heart Failure.
articles.abstract: Heart failure (HF) remains a major global health challenge, with high morbidity, frequent hospitalization, and substantial mortality despite major advances in guideline-directed therapy. Landmark EMPEROR-Reduced and EMPEROR-Preserved trials established empagliflozin, a sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitor (SGLT2i), as an effective therapy across the spectrum of HF, independent of diabetes status. However, the molecular mechanisms underlying its cardioprotective effects remain incompletely understood. Growing experimental and translational evidences suggest that restoration of myocardial sodium (Na+) and calcium (Ca2+) homeostasis represents a key mechanism. In failing cardiomyocytes, intracellular Na+ and Ca2+ overload, leading to impaired excitation-contraction coupling, mitochondrial dysfunction, oxidative stress, electrical instability, and adverse ventricular remodeling. Empagliflozin appears to interrupt this pathological cascade by limiting pathological Na+ entry, attenuating late sodium current (INa-L) and sodium-hydrogen exchanger 1 (NHE1) activity, modulating Ca2+/calmodulin-dependent protein kinase II (CaMKII) signaling, improving Na+-Ca2+ exchanger (NCX)-mediated Ca2+ handling, and preserving mitochondrial ion homeostasis. This review summarizes current evidence linking empagliflozin to myocardial Na+-Ca2+ homeostasis, discusses the integration of ion-handling mechanisms with its established clinical benefits, highlights unresolved mechanistic controversies, and outlines priorities for future basic and translational research.

articles.title: Research Progress of Astragali Complanati Semen Based on Bibliometric Analysis: Herbal Textual Research, Processing, Chemical Constituents, and Pharmacological Activities.
articles.abstract: ETHNOPHARMACOLOGICAL RELEVANCE: Astragali Complanati Semen (ACS), the dried mature seeds of Astragalus complanatus R. Br., is a traditional Chinese medicine with a long history of medicinal use. According to traditional Chinese medicinal records, ACS is traditionally used for tonifying the kidney and strengthening yang, consolidating essence and reducing urinary frequency, and nourishing the liver and improving visual function. Modern phytochemical and pharmacological studies have revealed that ACS contains various bioactive constituents, including flavonoids, triterpenoid saponins, amino acids, fatty acids, sterols, sesquiterpenoids, polysaccharides, and trace elements, which may contribute to its traditional therapeutic applications. AIM OF THE STUDY: This review aimed to identify research trends and hotspots in ACS and to summarize its geo-authenticity, processing methods, chemical constituents, pharmacological activities, mechanisms, and future prospects. MATERIALS AND METHODS: Bibliometric visualization was performed using publications retrieved from the China National Knowledge Infrastructure (CNKI), Wanfang Data Knowledge Service Platform (Wanfang), VIP Chinese Science and Technology Journal Database (VIP), Web of Science (WoS), and PubMed. The findings were integrated with a comprehensive review of herbal textual research, processing, chemical constituents, pharmacological effects, and mechanisms. RESULTS: The number of publications increased steadily, with China accounting for the largest share. Institutions from 28 Chinese provinces and municipalities contributed, with Shaanxi Province showing the highest publication frequency. Research hotspots included geo-authenticity, processing, chemical constituents, pharmacological activities, and mechanisms. ACS contains diverse chemical constituents, including flavonoids, sesquiterpenoids, triterpenoid saponins, polysaccharides, and other constituents. Major pharmacological activities include antihypertensive, lipid-lowering, hepatoprotective, antifibrotic, antioxidant, and anti-inflammatory effects. CONCLUSIONS: This review clarifies ACS research trends and hotspots and comprehensively summarizes its major research domains. Future studies should focus on quality markers (Q-markers), the activities and mechanisms of flavonoid monomers, and the isolation, purification, structural characterization, and structure-activity relationships of polysaccharides.

articles.title: The global extent of polypharmacy in neonatal intensive care: A systematic review.
articles.abstract: AIMS: Pharmaceutical treatment in the neonatal intensive care unit (NICU) is challenging, with neonates often receiving multiple drugs during hospitalization. Given their physiological immaturity, polypharmacy raises concerns about potential adverse effects, drug-drug interactions and the risk of supratherapeutic or subtherapeutic treatment. However, the extent and patterns of drug utilization in NICUs remain underexplored. Accordingly, this study aims to systematically summarise existing literature on polypharmacy in NICUs worldwide. METHODS: This systematic review, registered in PROSPERO, adhered to PRISMA guidelines. A structured search in EMBASE, Medline and CINAHL identified NICU drug utilization studies (2014-2024). Study selection followed a two-step screening process using the PICO framework. Two reviewers independently screened articles, extracted data and assessed quality with the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale. RESULTS: We included 40 studies across 17 countries, with India and Brazil most frequently represented. Cohorts varied widely, with sample sizes ranging from 41 to 799 016. Polypharmacy was prevalent, particularly among preterm neonates. Commonly prescribed drugs were anti-infectives, respiratory agents and gastrointestinal/metabolic medications. Methodological inconsistencies and variability in medication classification complicated accurate quantification of polypharmacy. CONCLUSIONS: This review highlights the widespread use of polypharmacy in NICUs globally, yet few studies comprehensively assess the full scope and impact of polypharmacy. The lack of detailed data on drug indications, dosages, treatment duration and adverse effects limits the ability to evaluate the safety and clinical consequences of polypharmacy. Data collection resulting in standardized methodologies are essential to advancing neonatal pharmacotherapy ensuring safer medication use in this vulnerable population.

articles.title: Are pregnancy- and lactation-related eligibility criteria in cardiovascular clinical trials underpinned by drug safety data?
articles.abstract: AIM: To quantify the prevalence of pregnancy-, lactation- and reproductive potential-related eligibility criteria in cardiovascular clinical trials and to evaluate whether they are supported by drug-specific safety data. METHODS: We analysed randomized phase 3 and phase 4 cardiovascular clinical trials registered on ClinicalTrials.gov between 1 January 2004 and 31 December 2023. We used a rule-based natural language processing approach to identify eligibility criteria related to pregnancy, lactation and reproductive potential. In trials evaluating antihypertensive and lipid-modifying drugs, criteria were assessed against human safety data. RESULTS: Among 1346 trials (1 834 685 participants, 37% women), 64% contained pregnancy-, lactation- or reproductive potential-related eligibility criteria. Pregnancy-related criteria occurred in 59% of trials, lactation-related criteria in 41% and reproductive potential-related criteria in 35%. These criteria frequently overlapped. In the 166 trials evaluating antihypertensive and lipid-modifying drugs, 133 (80%) excluded pregnant women, with 62% of these exclusions being supported by safety data. The remaining 51 (38%) were unsupported because human safety data were insufficient. For lactation, 9 of 97 exclusions (9%) were supported by safety data, 23 (24%) were unsupported because the drug was considered safe and 65 (67%) were unsupported due to insufficient safety data. CONCLUSION: Pregnancy-, lactation- and reproductive potential-related eligibility criteria are common in cardiovascular trials. Many exclusions of pregnant or lactating women were not supported by drug-specific safety data, particularly for lactation. Continued exclusion in the absence of sufficient safety data limits opportunities to generate evidence within the controlled setting of clinical trials, shifting evidence generation to routine clinical practice.

articles.title: H3K9 lactylation transcriptionally activates EHMT2 to drive pulmonary arterial hypertension via PPARγ repression.
articles.abstract: Pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH) is characterized by excessive proliferation and migration of pulmonary arterial smooth muscle cells (PASMCs), yet how hypoxia-associated metabolic reprogramming contributes to pulmonary vascular remodeling remains unclear. Here, we show that hypoxia elevates intracellular lactate in PASMCs, promoting HBO1 (lysine acetyltransferase 7/KAT7)-catalyzed H3K9 lactylation (H3K9la) at the EHMT2 promoter and enhancing EHMT2 transcription. Smooth muscle cell-specific Ehmt2 deletion attenuates pulmonary vascular remodeling and right ventricular hypertrophy in SU5416/hypoxia (SuHx) mice and suppresses PASMC proliferation and migration. Conversely, EHMT2 overexpression promotes these phenotypes and mediates lactate-induced PASMC dysfunction. RNA sequencing of pulmonary arteries from Ehmt2-deficient mice identifies PPARγ repression as a downstream mechanism. EHMT2 inhibits PPARγ nuclear translocation, whereas rosiglitazone ameliorates EHMT2-induced PASMC dysfunction. Moreover, administration of lactate exacerbates SuHx-induced PAH in an EHMT2-dependent manner. Collectively, these findings identify a lactate-H3K9la-EHMT2-PPARγ axis linking hypoxia-induced metabolic reprogramming to pulmonary vascular remodeling and PAH progression.

articles.title: Tectoridin Attenuates Alzheimer's Pathology by Inhibiting Aβ Aggregation in 3xTg-AD Mice.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Alzheimer's disease (AD) remains a major neurodegenerative challenge, necessitating the development of innovative, mechanism-targeted therapies. PURPOSE: Tectoridin (Tec), an isoflavone from Belamcanda chinensis (L.) DC., was systematically investigated for its novel neuroprotective effects in AD to elucidate its therapeutic potential and molecular mechanisms. METHODS: In vitro, western blotting, calcium assays, and flow cytometry were used to characterize Tec's impact on neuronal homeostasis. In vivo, the therapeutic efficacy of Tec was assessed in 3xTg-AD mice. Cognitive performance was evaluated via the Morris Water Maze, while pathological changes were analyzed through immunohistochemistry. RNA sequencing and experimental validation were performed to delineate regulatory pathways. RESULT: Tec effectively inhibited Aβ aggregation and exhibited potent antioxidant activity. It maintained cellular homeostasis by mitigating Aβ-induced calcium overload, restoring ATP levels, and stabilizing mitochondrial membrane potential, ultimately preventing neuronal apoptosis. Furthermore, Tec treatment significantly ameliorated cognitive impairments in 3xTg-AD mice and markedly reduced cerebral Aβ plaque deposition. Mechanistic analysis revealed that Tec improves AD pathology by upregulating LRP1, thereby promoting the transmembrane transport and systemic clearance of Aβ. CONCLUSION: This study confirms that Tec exerts significant neuroprotective effects in AD by inhibiting Aβ aggregation, reducing neuronal apoptosis and upregulating the expression of LRP1. The upregulation of LRP1 by Tec may enhance Aβ efflux from the brain, thereby contributing to the reduced Aβ pathology and subsequent neuroprotection observed in this study. In summary, tectoridin is a promising natural therapeutic for AD due to its high safety and multi-target mechanisms.

articles.title: Sinomenine prevents monocrotaline-induced pulmonary arterial hypertension by inhibiting osteopontin-mediated PASMC phenotypic switching.
articles.abstract: Pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH) is a life-threatening disease driven by progressive pulmonary vascular remodeling, and aberrant phenotypic transition of pulmonary arterial smooth muscle cells (PASMCs) serves as the core pathological driver of disease deterioration. Sinomenine (SIN), a structurally defined isoquinoline alkaloid isolated from Sinomenium acutum (Thunb.) Rehder & E.H.Wilson, exhibits anti-inflammatory, vascular-protective, and anti-remodeling activities. Nevertheless, the exact molecular mechanism by which SIN regulates PASMC dysfunction to prevent PAH remains unclear. In vivo, SIN administration significantly attenuated MCT-induced PAH, right ventricular hypertrophy and pulmonary vascular remodeling in rats. In vitro, SIN effectively suppressed platelet-derived growth factor-BB (PDGF-BB)-triggered proliferation, migration and phenotypic switching of PASMCs. RNA-sequencing coupled with KEGG enrichment analysis further identified the ECM-receptor interaction pathway as the key signaling cascade dysregulated by MCT, with osteopontin (OPN) validated as the central functional target of SIN. OPN overexpression recapitulated the pro-remodeling effects of PDGF-BB in PASMCs, and such abnormal phenotypes were prevented by SIN. Molecular docking and cellular thermal shift assay demonstrated that SIN binds to NF-κB, a transcription factor of OPN, and suppresses PDGF-BB-induced NF-κB activation. This study uncovers a novel mechanism of SIN against PAH and highlights OPN as a critical mediator of its protective effects.

articles.title: Sofalcone, a mucoprotective drug, inhibits platelet activation and arterial thrombosis.
articles.abstract: Gastrointestinal injury remains a major limitation of aspirin-based antiplatelet therapy. Sofalcone is a clinically used mucoprotective drug with an established safety profile, but its effects on platelet function remain unclear. This study aims to evaluate the antiplatelet effects of sofalcone and elucidate its underlying mechanisms. In human platelets, sofalcone inhibited platelet adhesion on collagen and suppressed aggregation and secretion induced by U46619, collagen, and arachidonic acid. It converted ADP-induced irreversible aggregation into a reversible response while minimally affecting thrombin-induced aggregation or coagulation parameters. Sofalcone did not alter TXA2 production or activate cyclic AMP or cyclic GMP signaling. Instead, it produced rightward shifts in U46619 concentration-response curves and attenuated TP receptor-mediated Ca2+ mobilization in platelets and TP-expressing HEK293T cells. Docking analysis suggested interaction with the TP receptor binding pocket. Notably, a long half-life major metabolite of sofalcone displayed slightly greater antiplatelet potency. Under whole blood flow conditions, sofalcone and its metabolite reduced thrombus formation on collagen-coated microfluidic chamber surfaces. Combination treatment with sofalcone and either aspirin or ticagrelor further enhanced the inhibition of platelet aggregation and thrombus formation. In mice, intraperitoneal or oral sofalcone prevented FeCl3-induced arterial thrombosis without prolonging tail bleeding time. Together, these findings support the potential repurposing of sofalcone as an alternative or adjunctive antiplatelet therapy, particularly in settings where gastrointestinal protection is clinically desirable.

articles.title: Prostaglandin-Endoperoxide Synthase 1 Regulatory Variants Link Aspirin-Treated Cardiovascular Outcomes to Multicellular Cyclooxygenase-1 Expression and Activity Beyond Platelet-Derived Cyclooxygenase-1 Inhibition.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Prostaglandin-endoperoxide synthase 1 (PTGS1) encodes cyclooxygenase-1 (COX-1). Aspirin inhibits platelet COX-1/thromboxane A2 (TXA2)-dependent aggregation to prevent major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE). However, relationships of low aspirin response, namely laboratory aspirin resistance (LAR) and MACE, with PTGS1 variants remain uncertain. METHODS: In total, 486 cardiovascular patients, 454 on mono-antiplatelet therapy (MAPT), 32 on dual antiplatelet therapy (DAPT, aspirin plus clopidogrel), had complete data including COX-1-specific platelet function and median 4.75-year follow-up. MACE comprised acute myocardial infarction, acute stroke, and ischemia-driven revascularization. Eighteen bioinformatically annotated PTGS1 regulatory variants were genotyped. RESULTS: Smoking and clopidogrel exposure significantly modified LAR. Kaplan-Meier analysis linked LAR to higher crude MACE odds in MAPT and MAPT+DAPT groups (log-rank P < 0.05). Genetic analyses clarified gene-LAR, gene-MACE, gene-LAR-MACE interrelationships. Promoter rs1330344 showed lower LAR odds, with unchanged MACE odds, consistent with mild COX-1 modulation. Intronic rs7866582 conferred higher MACE odds alone, consistent with leukocyte COX-1/proinflammatory prostaglandin elevation. 3'-untranslated region (3'-UTR) rs10306190 exhibited marginally higher LAR odds yet lower MACE odds, consistent with variant-mediated COX-1 upregulation and marked vascular COX-1/PGI2 elevation counteracting residual TXA2 under aspirin. 3'-UTR rs10306196 displayed higher MACE odds alone, consistent with marked vascular COX-1/PGI2 reduction (nominal Firth P < 0.05, except for rs10306190-LAR). However, after multiple testing correction, no significant associations were observed (all BH-FDR Q > 0.05). CONCLUSIONS: LAR and PTGS1 variants lack population-level value for MACE prediction. This study links aspirin-treated MACE to multicellular COX-1 actions beyond platelets.

articles.title: Assessment of Δ9-tetrahydrocannabiphorol (THCP), Δ8-tetrahydrocannabinol (Δ8-THC), and cannabinol (CBN) pharmacodynamics and pharmacokinetics across multiple routes of administration in the C57BL/6 mouse.
articles.abstract: Δ9-Tetrahydrocannabinol (Δ9-THC), along with the non-intoxicating cannabinoid cannabidiol (CBD), is one of the most-abundant phytocannabinoids in the Cannabis sativa plant after decarboxylation of its acid form. Other phytocannabinoids present in limited quantities that may also be psychotropic, specifically Δ9-tetrahydrocannabiphorol (THCP), Δ8-tetrahydrocannabinol (Δ8-THC), and cannabinol (CBN). Compared to Δ9-THC, relatively little is known about their properties, yet these compounds are increasingly available in cannabis products. There is a pressing need to better understand the pharmacology of these phytocannabinoids and their potential health risks. In the present study, male and female mice were treated with THCP, Δ8-THC, or CBN via tail vein intravenous injection, intraperitoneal injection, or oral gavage and their levels were measured in whole-blood to estimate pharmacokinetic parameters while also measuring catalepsy, body temperature, and nociception. Catalepsy, body temperature, nociception, and locomotion were further assessed in male and female mice receiving Δ8-THC or CBN by intracranial injection. THCP levels were relatively high in blood and rapidly eliminated, whereas Δ8-THC and CBN pharmacokinetics were similar, compared to past studies using Δ9-THC. When accounting for circulating compound levels and ED50 responses, THCP was a highly potent and efficacious inducer of catalepsy, hypothermia, and reduced nociception, while Δ8-THC and CBN displayed limited activity, consistent with others' findings. Intracranial administration of Δ8-THC or CBN produced significant catalepsy or reduced nociception, respectively. This study presents the relative potencies and pharmacokinetic properties of THCP, Δ8-THC, and CBN in mice, that suggest that compared to Δ9-THC, THCP is more intoxicating, whereas Δ8-THC and CBN may be less-so.

articles.title: Oleanolic acid induces STING-dependent ferroptosis in hepatocellular carcinoma by promoting mitochondrial DNA leakage and targeting STING.
articles.abstract: Oleanolic acid (OA) has anti-hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) effects, but the underlying mechanisms remain incompletely understood. Ferroptosis, a type of regulated cell death that depends on iron, offers a hopeful therapeutic target in HCC. In this study, we identify a heretofore unrecognized mechanism by which OA, a natural pentacyclic triterpenoid, exerts potent anti-HCC activity through the induction of STING-dependent ferroptosis. We herein provide the first evidence that OA-induced mitochondrial damage leads to the efflux of mtDNA into the cytosol. Once released, this mtDNA functions as an endogenous danger-associated molecular pattern to activate STING signaling, which in turn precipitates a cascade of ferroptotic events-including lipid peroxidation, ferrous iron accumulation, and GSH depletion-observed consistently across in vitro and in vivo settings. Crucially, STING knockdown significantly attenuates OA-induced ferroptosis and abrogates its antitumor efficacy, establishing STING as a functional mediator of OA activity. Moreover, we provide the evidence that OA binds to STING protein, enhancing its protein stability by suppressing ubiquitin-proteasome-mediated degradation. Collectively, our findings uncover a dual mechanism of action for OA: it acts as an upstream trigger of mtDNA-driven STING activation and as a pharmacological stabilizer of STING. This study not only reveals a novel mechanistic link between mtDNA/STING signaling and ferroptosis in HCC but also identifies STING as a previously unrecognized target of OA, positioning OA as a promising lead compound for HCC therapy.

articles.title: Lipid nanoparticles adjuvanted with poly(I:C) enhance respiratory mucosal immunity induced by a protein subunit vaccine.
articles.abstract: Subunit vaccines are typically given through injections, which limits mucosal immunity. Most adjuvants do not stimulate mucosal responses but using lipid nanoparticles (LNPs) encapsulating polyinosinic-polycytidylic acid (poly(I:C)), a toll-like receptor 3 agonist, could enhance the immune response in the lungs. We tested LNPs made from four ionizable lipids using a microfluidic mixing method to encapsulate poly(I:C) at different concentrations. The LNPs were evaluated for particle size, polydispersity index (PDI), poly(I:C) encapsulation efficiency (EE %), morphology, and NF-κB activation over a 4-week period. Mice were immunized with LNPs containing poly(I:C) and a protein antigen from Mycobacterium tuberculosis via the intrapulmonary route. Results showed that LNPs formulated with low molecular weight poly(I:C) exhibited the most favorable physicochemical properties and higher NF-κB induction compared to those made with high molecular weight poly(I:C), although a statistically significant difference was only observed for PDI. LNPs made with the ionizable lipid SM-102 were the most stable. Immunized mice had enhanced levels of serum and mucosal antibodies. Notably, the most prominent effect of the poly(I:C)-LNPs was the generation of significant cytokine-producing cells in the lungs and spleen, alongside memory cells in the lungs, spleen, and lymph nodes. In conclusion, pulmonary immunization with poly(I:C)-LNPs induced both systemic and mucosal immunity, though further investigation into antigen-specific protection is necessary. Overall, this work demonstrates new possibilities for vaccine development against respiratory infections.

articles.title: Filament-based bezoar structures as a pathophysiological inspired concept for gastroretentive drug delivery: Integration of material design and biorelevant mechanical in vitro testing.
articles.abstract: Achieving reliable gastric retention remains one of the key unsolved challenges in oral drug delivery. Conventional gastroretentive approaches - such as floating, expanding, or mucoadhesive systems - often fail to withstand the complex mechanical forces of the stomach, leading to inconsistent residence times and unpredictable drug release, especially in the fasting state. Inspired by the natural persistence of trichobezoars, this work introduces filament-based "bezoar-like" structures as a novel, pathophysiological inspired concept for gastroretentive drug delivery. Multifilament polymer fibers were produced by hot-melt extrusion and assembled into spherical bezoars capable of resisting peristaltic propulsion while allowing controlled drug release. To capture the interplay between material properties and gastric motility, a comprehensive in vitro framework was established combining texture analysis, a modified antrum model, and stress-based dissolution testing. These methods reproduce physiologically relevant compression, shear, and retropulsion events that are absent from conventional compendial apparatuses. The study demonstrates that integrating structural design with biorelevant mechanical testing enables more realistic assessment of gastroretentive performance. The proposed filament-based systems mimic key viscoelastic features of natural hair-like bezoars and withstand simulated gastric motility while maintaining sustained release characteristics. This concept provides a new paradigm for designing robust gastroretentive dosage forms and highlights the need for mechanical stress-adapted in vitro methods as a prerequisite for meaningful in vivo translation.

articles.title: Handling and administration of paediatric mini-tablets: considerations for dose measurement and dispensing.
articles.abstract: The development of minitablets (MTs) for children is gaining interest due to their superior stability and lower bulk compared to oral liquids. Despite MTs offering opportunities for flexible individualised dosing, most MT products are presented as unit-dose packs. The findings of Company internal MT handling, assessment, and human factors studies that evaluated unit dose stick packs, handling aids such as scoops, and proprietary and prototype MT counting aids were interrogated to identify key themes and inform decisions regarding MT dose dispensing options. The usability and suitability of dispensing options depended on properties of the MTs, number per dose and dose range. Although study designs were diverse, the results suggested that where fully flexible individualised dosing is required, up to eight minitablets may be counted in a single manual counting operation with the use of a handling aid, whilst larger quantities would likely require the use of a minitablet counting aid. For drug products where dose-banding is permitted, the use of unit dose packs may be the most favourable approach if fill accuracy can be assured. However, selection of dispensing approach should be made on a product case-by-case basis: a decision tree is proposed to facilitate the selection process.
authors: On behalf for the European Paediatric Formulation Initiative EuPFI

articles.title: pH-responsive fmoc-FF nanogels entrap internalized cargo within endosomes, preventing its trafficking to lysosomes.
articles.abstract: Nanocarriers have become central tools in modern nanomedicine, enabling the intracellular delivery of therapeutic molecules that would otherwise be rapidly degraded or poorly internalized. Most nanocarriers internalized by endocytosis are sorted to the lysosomes, where acidification and enzymatic activity restrict bioavailability of their cargo. Trapping cargo in a pre-lysosomal compartment might result beneficial for successful intracellular delivery. Fmoc-FF nanogels are supramolecularly assembled, tunable carriers whose behavior responds to changes in the local chemical environment. Here, we characterize their intracellular trafficking and show that Fmoc-FF nanogels enter cells predominantly through caveolae-mediated endocytosis and accumulate within EEA1-positive early endosomes. Unlike conventional polymeric nanoparticles, these nanogels do not progress toward lysosomes. Instead, Fmoc-FF nanogels are associated with impaired early endosomal maturation, pronounced vesicle enlargement, and membrane destabilization. Acridine orange redistribution confirms loss of endosomal structure. In vitro data suggest that endosomal pH might drive structural rearrangement of the nanogel. Together, our findings demonstrate that Fmoc-FF nanogels profoundly remodel the endosomal network, altering endosomal trafficking and cargo processing, and highlight their potential as intracellular delivery platforms.

articles.title: Carbon monoxide-releasing mesoporous polydopamine nanoplatform for lysosomal disruption and synergistic tumor therapy.
articles.abstract: Lysosomes, pivotal in tumor progression and therapy resistance, sustain cancer survival through drug tolerance and stress adaptation. Conventional lysosome-disrupting approaches faced transient efficacy from poor targeting or cellular repair mechanisms. To address this, we engineered a biomimetic nanoplatform (FeCO@MP-P) integrating polydopamine's pH/photothermal responsiveness with gas-generating FeCO and charge-reversal PEOz coating. The charge-reversal strategy enhanced cellular uptake by 1.8-fold. Subsequently, the combined application of multiple lysosome-disrupting strategies achieved efficient lysosomal damage. Following cellular internalization, FeCO@MP-P initially accumulated in lysosomes, where H2O2-responsive CO release, Fe-mediated ROS generation, and NIR-induced photothermal stress collectively contributed to lysosomal damage. Subsequent cytoplasmic redistribution further amplified intracellular oxidative stress, mitochondrial dysfunction, and apoptosis. Ultimately, FeCO@MP-P suppressed approximately 95% of tumor growth. This study pioneers a lysosome-targeted strategy that couples irreversible organelle disruption with ROS potentiation, demonstrating a paradigm to subvert adaptive tumor defenses through mechanistically synchronized nanomaterials.

articles.title: Development and evaluation of inhalable imipenem dry powder for treating pulmonary P. aeruginosa infection.
articles.abstract: Pulmonary infections caused by P. aeruginosa (PA) remain a major clinical challenge due to biofilm formation, intrinsic resistance, and limited antibiotic penetration into lung tissues following systemic administration. Imipenem (IPM), a broad-spectrum carbapenem, requires high intravenous doses (500 mg every 6 h with cilastatin) to achieve therapeutic lung levels, leading to frequent dosing and systemic toxicity. Pulmonary delivery via dry powder for inhalation (DPI) offers a targeted alternative. However, formulation development is hindered by the chemical instability, specifically its susceptibility to thermal and hydrolytic degradation in the amorphous state. In this study, a high-dose, chemically stable IPM dry powder for inhalation (IPM-DPI) was developed by co-spray-drying IPM with L-leucine. The optimized 50:50 (w/w) IPM: L-leucine powder exhibited an initial IPM potency of ∼94% and low residual moisture content (<2% w/w). Differential scanning calorimetry and powder X-ray diffraction of IPM-DPI confirmed amorphous IPM and semi-crystalline L-leucine, while Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy suggested intermolecular interactions between IPM and L-leucine. The IPM-DPI demonstrated excellent aerosolization, achieving fine particle fractions of ∼67% (Orbital™ DPI) and ∼53% (RS01® DPI), with a mass median aerodynamic diameter of 2.4-3.2 µm and retained antimicrobial potency (minimum inhibitory concentration of 0.125-0.25 µg/mL). IPM-DPI maintained >95% of its initial IPM potency after 6 months at -20 °C, demonstrating improved stability associated with intermolecular interactions between leucine and IMP, with the semi-crystalline leucine phase forming a matrix around IMP molecules within the particle core. Overall, the developed IPM-DPI enables localized pulmonary delivery of imipenem, potentially eliminating the need for cilastatin and reducing systemic toxicity associated with parenteral therapy.

articles.title: Comparative selection of cell-penetrating peptides and development of D-Arg9/iRGD dual-functionalized triptolide nanoliposomes for deepened penetration and rheumatoid arthritis therapy.
articles.abstract: Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) nanodelivery remains limited by insufficient cellular uptake and restricted penetration into deeper tissue regions. In this study, five cell-penetrating peptides (CPPs), including L-TAT, L-MPG, L-Lys9, L-Arg9, and D-Arg9, were comparatively evaluated using a unified liposomal platform. Coumarin 6 (C6) was used as a fluorescent tracer to characterize cellular uptake, subcellular fluorescence distribution, and responses of CPP-functionalized liposomes to endocytic inhibitors, while the corresponding triptolide (TP)-loaded formulations were examined for in vitro anti-inflammatory activity and in vivo anti-arthritic efficacy. During the early incubation period, D-Arg9@LipoC6 exhibited relatively high intracellular C6 fluorescence and a broader subcellular distribution. D-Arg9@LipoTP reduced intracellular reactive oxygen species (ROS) and multiple pro-inflammatory mediators, together with decreased CD86 expression, increased CD206 expression, and modulation of NF-κB-related protein expression. D-Arg9 was subsequently combined with the tissue-penetrating peptide iRGD to generate D-Arg9-iRGD@LipoTP. In three-dimensional RAW264.7 spheroids, D-Arg9-iRGD@LipoC6 retained stronger C6 fluorescence in deeper spheroid regions and displayed a broader spatial distribution than either D-Arg9@LipoC6 or iRGD@LipoC6. The corresponding TP-loaded formulation reduced TNF-α, IL-6, IL-1β, and PGE2 levels while increasing IL-10 levels. Following intra-articular administration in rats with adjuvant-induced arthritis (AIA), D-Arg9-iRGD@LipoTP attenuated paw swelling, increased the thermal pain threshold, and alleviated joint inflammation, cartilage damage, and bone destruction. No consistent abnormalities were detected in the measured serum biochemical parameters, and hematoxylin and eosin (H&E) examination of major organs revealed no evident histopathological lesions. C6 was used solely as a tracer of formulation-associated fluorescence distribution; accordingly, intracellular and spheroid C6 fluorescence should not be interpreted as a direct measure of TP exposure. These findings suggest that D-Arg9 enhances liposomal cellular uptake, whereas the incorporation of iRGD further improves distribution into deeper regions of dense three-dimensional tissue-like structures, supporting a peptide-functionalization strategy for concurrently improving cellular uptake and intratissue distribution in local nanodelivery for RA.

articles.title: Automated Extrusion-based Dispensing of Mucoadhesive Oral Films Containing Buprenorphine for Feline Delivery to the Gingiva.
articles.abstract: Cats are undertreated patients due to their lack of communication, with limited options for oral pain management, and may benefit from individualized oral dosage forms to facilitate at-home pain management. Buprenorphine would be a suitable treatment option with a proven safety profile. It is readily absorbed across the oral mucosa and acts, therefore, systemically. Extemporaneous formulations can be administered buccally to enable at-home treatment of pain, yet the poor palatability of formulations and highly variable absorption limit therapeutic effectiveness and regular clinical translation. However, preparing appropriately sized dosage forms for buprenorphine administration remains challenging. This study evaluated automated extrusion-based dispensing (AED), a simplified extrusion-based 3D printing, as an approach for preparing personalized mucoadhesive oral films (MFs) containing buprenorphine hydrochloride for gingival application in feline analgesia. A formulation consisting of CMC-Na, PEG 400, and water was identified as suitable for AED. The resulting films showed reproducible mass, uniform drug content, suitable pH, and rapid disintegration and drug release. In a preliminary administration trial with 39 cats, placebo MFs were retained at the gingival mucosa and were well accepted, supporting the feasibility of gingival application. Overall, AED enabled the preparation of personalized MFs for feline gingival administration, providing a basis for further development and evaluation of this dosage form.

articles.title: Formononetin disrupts MRSA biofilm via potential SarA-associated regulatory modulation.
articles.abstract: Biofilm formation is a crucial aspect of Methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) pathogenesis and contributes to its resistance against conventional antibiotics. This study reports the identification of a bioactive molecule, formononetin, from Glycyrrhiza glabra L., that is effective against MRSA. Formononetin significantly inhibited biofilm formation, disrupted sessile biofilm, and reduced the hemolytic activity of MRSA in a dose-dependent manner. Formononetin also increased the survival rate of MRSA-infected G. mellonella larvae by decreasing the bacterial load and increasing melanization. The combination of formononetin with antibiotics, like oxacillin, ampicillin, and streptomycin, showed a fractional inhibitory concentration index (FICI) ≤ 0.5, which indicates a synergistic effect. Molecular docking studies showed formononetin can bind to the global regulator, SarA, with an estimated binding score of -6.176 kcal/mol. Further, the aspartate residue (D20) in SarA was identified as a binding site for formononetin. Microscale thermophoresis and electrophoretic mobility shift assay of the SarAD20A mutant showed reduced affinity towards formononetin without affecting its DNA-binding activity compared to its wild-type counterpart. Further, proteomic profiling of MRSA upon treatment with formononetin showed significant modulation of SarA and SarA-related pathways, such as scdA and agrC. Our findings suggest that formononetin holds promise as a natural agent for combating MRSA biofilm.

articles.title: A self-assembling coculture model of retinal fibrosis reveals Bcl-xL inhibitors as cell-selective dual-mechanism antifibrotics.
articles.abstract: Retinal fibrosis contributes to vision loss in multiple chronic and acute retinal diseases, impacting millions of patients; however, no effective antifibrotic interventions exist. To model retinal fibrosis, we created a self-assembling, coculture model using retinal pigment epithelial (RPE) and Müller cells stimulated with a transforming growth factor-β2 and fibroblast growth factor 2 cocktail to recapitulate the fibrotic milieu. High-content imaging of fibronectin and α-smooth muscle actin enabled quantitative assessment of fibrotic responses. Using this platform, we confirmed that current anti-vascular endothelial growth factor therapies had no measurable effect on fibrosis and evaluated a panel of proposed antifibrotic targets, which showed limited potency and translational potential. In a pilot screen of novel retinal antifibrotic candidates, Bcl-xL (BCL2L1) emerged as a highly promising target. Treatment with the clinical candidate UBX-1325 promoted apoptosis selectively in activated α-smooth muscle actin-expressing Müller cells, while simultaneously blocking fibrotic activation in RPE cells through a noncanonical, apoptosis-independent mechanism. Analysis of patient-derived retinal membranes revealed elevated BCL2L1 expression in proliferative vitreoretinopathy membranes compared with epiretinal membranes, supporting the clinical relevance of this target. Together, these findings identify Bcl-xL as a potent, dual-action target for retinal fibrosis and highlight UBX-1325 as a promising candidate for translation. SIGNIFICANCE STATEMENT: Using a self-assembling retinal fibrosis model, this study demonstrated that currently available anti-vascular endothelial growth factor therapies lack direct antifibrotic activity and identify Bcl-xL as a promising therapeutic target. The clinical-stage molecule UBX-1325 suppresses fibrosis through complementary effects on Müller and RPE cells, providing a strong rationale for clinical evaluation in fibrotic retinal diseases.

articles.title: The role of central monoamines in the positive reinforcing effects of affective touch.
articles.abstract: RATIONALE: Affective touch can produce positive emotional states and serves as a critical component of social bonding. Although the circuitry of affective touch has been well characterized, the role of central monoamines in the functional consequences of affective touch has not been systematically examined. OBJECTIVES: The objective of this study was to examine the role of monoamines in the positive reinforcing effects of affective touch METHODS: Male and female rats were treated with selective monoamine reuptake inhibitors (GBR 12909, atomoxetine, fluoxetine) and nonselective monoamine releasers/reuptake inhibitors (amphetamine, cocaine, MDMA) and placed into an apparatus divided into two equally sized areas. When rats were in the "touch" area, they were "petted" by a blinded experimenter; when rats were in the "no touch" area, they were left undisturbed. All drugs were tested across a 10-fold dose range, and saline and oxytocin were tested as negative and positive controls, respectively. RESULTS: Affective touch served as a positive reinforcer as indicated by a preference for the "touch" area. Oxytocin, the nonselective monoamine reuptake inhibitor cocaine, and the nonselective monoamine releaser amphetamine robustly increased the reinforcing effects of touch. To a lesser degree, the selective dopamine reuptake inhibitor GBR 12909 increased the reinforcing effects of touch, whereas the nonselective monoamine releaser/reuptake inhibitor MDMA decreased the reinforcing effects of touch. CONCLUSIONS: These data suggest that drugs that increase synaptic dopamine, particularly those with high addiction liability, increase the positive reinforcing effects of affective touch. These data also suggest that MDMA may not reproduce in rodents the entactogenic effects commonly reported in humans and some nonhuman primate studies.

articles.title: EGFR-targeted drugs and resistance mechanisms in non-small cell lung cancer: Molecular insights and emerging therapeutic strategies.
articles.abstract: Epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) plays a pivotal role in the pathogenesis and progression of non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), with activating mutations serving as key determinants of sensitivity to targeted therapies. The prevalence and spectrum of EGFR mutations are influenced by histology, ethnicity, and environmental factors, encompassing common alterations such as exon 19 deletions and the L858R point mutation, as well as uncommon variants including exon 20 insertions, kinase domain duplications, and other rare substitutions. These molecular distinctions underlie differential responses to first-, second-, and third-generation tyrosine kinase inhibitors (TKIs), emphasizing the necessity of precise molecular profiling for individualized treatment selection. Although EGFR TKIs initially produce robust responses, resistance inevitably develops via on-target mutations (e.g., T790M, C797S), activation of bypass signaling pathways, co-occurring genetic alterations, and histologic or phenotypic transformation, challenging long-term disease control. Contemporary strategies to overcome resistance include combination therapies integrating TKIs with MEK, MET, or AXL inhibitors, antibody-based therapeutics, bispecific antibodies, antibody-drug conjugates, and emerging multifunctional biologics. Additionally, immunomodulatory interventions and nanotechnology-based delivery systems enhance anti-tumor efficacy while mitigating resistance. Non-invasive monitoring techniques, such as liquid biopsies, circulating tumor DNA profiling, and advanced imaging modalities, enable longitudinal assessment of mutation dynamics and therapeutic response, informing adaptive, precision-guided treatment strategies. This review synthesizes current knowledge on EGFR mutations, resistance mechanisms, and emerging therapeutic approaches in NSCLC, highlighting the integration of molecular, immunologic, and technological modalities to improve patient outcomes and advance precision oncology.

articles.title: The Association of Early Graft Dysfunction and CYP3A5 Genotype With Tacrolimus Exposure in Adult Kidney Transplant Recipients.
articles.abstract: INTRODUCTION: The incidence of early graft dysfunction following kidney transplantation is rising due to the expanded use of marginal organs. Prior studies have suggested that acute kidney dysfunction causes renohepatic crosstalk and tacrolimus metabolism may be decreased. It is also well known that tacrolimus metabolism and dosing requirements differ significantly based on a recipient's CYP3A5 genotype. The objective of this study was to investigate the interplay between early graft function and pharmacogenetics on tacrolimus dose requirements in adult kidney transplant recipients. METHODS: This was a single-center, retrospective cohort study of adult kidney transplant recipients who received immediate-release tacrolimus and had CYP3A5 genotypes available. Immediate graft function (IGF) was defined as serum creatinine decrease of ≥ 10% from baseline and urine output ≥ 0.5 mL/kg/h on post-operative day (POD) 1. Tacrolimus dose-normalized trough concentration (C/D) on POD 2 was compared between patients with IGF and non-IGF using Mann-Whitney U test. Patients were then grouped by both IGF and CYP3A5 genotype, and the differences in C/D considering these factors were analyzed by Mann Whitney U test and a multivariable linear regression analysis. RESULTS: A total of 242 patients were included, 185 with IGF and 57 with non-IGF. The median [IQR: interquartile range] of tacrolimus C/D was higher in non-IGF than IGF (200.0 [129.7-327.1] vs. 134.0 [95.0-197.4] [ng/ml]/[mg/kg/day], p < 0.001). Among CYP3A5 nonexpressers, the median [IQR] of tacrolimus C/D was 73% higher in non-IGF than IGF (263.3 [177.5-390.1] vs. 151.8 [105.1-214.1] [ng/ml]/[mg/kg/day], p < 0.001), and 16% higher in CYP3A5 expressers with non-IGF versus IGF (116.2 [102.3-199.5] vs. 101.1 [72.5-131.0] [ng/ml]/[mg/kg/day], p = 0.01). In the multivariable linear regression model, the effects of IGF and CYP3A5 expression on tacrolimus C/D remained significant. CONCLUSION: Patients with early graft dysfunction who were CYP3A5 nonexpressers had the highest tacrolimus exposure. Initial tacrolimus dose reductions may be considered in kidney transplant recipients who are at risk for non-IGF, especially in CYP3A5 nonexpressers.

articles.title: Gene-Dose Interaction in Low-Dose Irinotecan: A Real-World Cohort Study of the Association Between Adverse Effects and UGT1A1 Polymorphism.
articles.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Exposure to the toxic metabolite of irinotecan is higher in UGT1A1 poor metabolizers (PMs). It is uncertain if there is a higher risk for adverse effects in PMs receiving low-dose irinotecan regimens (< 150 mg/m2). In this retrospective cohort study, we examined in a real-world cohort the interaction between UGT1A1 polymorphism and initial irinotecan dose, with severe adverse effects of irinotecan. MATERIAL AND METHODS: We performed a retrospective cohort study based on Clalit Health Services (CHS) database, including all adults initiating irinotecan, with available UGT1A1 result. Short-term outcomes, within 2 months of first irinotecan dose, were Grade 3 or 4 neutropenia, hospitalization, and mortality. A composite outcome included all of the above. Secondary outcomes were hospitalization due to diarrhea and long-term overall survival. We used logistic regression models and a propensity score that included demographics, cancer-related variables, chronic clinical conditions, and laboratory characteristics at cohort entry. RESULT: Of 450 patients initiating irinotecan (2004-2025), 185 (41.1%) were UGT1A1 normal metabolizers (NMs), 211 (46.9%) were intermediate metabolizers (IMs), and 54 (12%) were PMs. Dosing data was available for 260 patients. UGT1A1 PM status was associated with increased risk for Grade-3 neutropenia with an odds ratio (OR) of 4.36 (95% CI 1.29-14.82) in the higher dose group, with a median initial dose (interquartile range) of 107 (100-115) mg/m2. UGT1A1 PM status was not associated with increased toxicity risk in the lower dose group, with a median initial dose (interquartile range) of 80 (66-88) mg/m2. The risk for the composite outcome in PMs receiving the higher dose had an OR of 3.19 (95% CI 0.95-10.72) p = 0.06 (marginally significant). An interaction between UGT1A1 polymorphism and initial irinotecan dose was identified. Propensity-score analysis and sensitivity analyses yielded similar results. There was no increased risk for hospitalizations due to diarrhea in PMs receiving higher doses of irinotecan, and no difference in overall survival was found between the four groups defined by polymorphism and initial dose. CONCLUSION: Our data suggest a possible dose-by-genotype interaction within the irinotecan regimens of < 150 mg/m2. The findings may support heightened vigilance and motivate larger prospective studies to establish the recommended initial irinotecan dose with regard to the common UGT1A1 polymorphism.

articles.title: Model-Informed First-In-Human Dose Selection for AZD2796, a High-Affinity Anti-LILRB2 Antibody.
articles.abstract: AZD2796 is a humanized anti-LILRB2 monoclonal antibody designed to promote immune activation by inhibiting LILRB2 on myeloid cells. Because AZD2796 does not bind cynomolgus monkey or rodent LILRB2, conventional approaches to first-in-human dose selection were limited. An affinity-based minimum anticipated biological effect level (MABEL) approach would predict a very low starting dose despite the potential for substantial target-mediated drug disposition (TMDD). To support dose selection, pharmacokinetic and receptor occupancy (PK-RO) models were developed using AZD2796 pharmacokinetics in cynomolgus monkeys and TMDD data estimated from a cynomolgus-reactive surrogate anti-LILRB2 antibody. An alternative approach using neonatal Fc receptor- and LILRB2-transgenic mouse models was also explored. The cynomolgus surrogate model predicted substantial TMDD at low doses and supported an intravenous starting dose of 30 mg every 3 weeks (Q3W) that was predicted to maintain peripheral LILRB2 occupancy. The model further predicted that approximately 300 mg Q3W would maintain > 95% tumor LILRB2 occupancy under conservative assumptions regarding target burden and tumor exposure. Model performance was supported by the model's ability to reproduce the clinically observed PK and RO characteristics of other anti-LILRB2 antibodies. The transgenic mouse approach was less robust and generally predicted higher dose requirements. These findings demonstrate that surrogate antibody PK-RO modeling can support the selection of a pharmacologically active first-in-human starting dose for therapeutic antibodies that lack cross-reactivity with standard preclinical species.

articles.title: Optimal Etomidate Induction Dosage Combined With Nerve Block Minimizes Postoperative Cognitive Dysfunction and Enhances Hemodynamic Stability in Elderly Hernia Patients.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Etomidate combined with nerve block is commonly used for elderly hernia surgery, but standardized dosing regimens remain lacking. OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to evaluate the effects of different induction doses of etomidate combined with nerve block on hemodynamic stability and cognitive function in elderly hernia patients, aiming to optimize the induction strategy. METHODS: 106 elderly patients scheduled for elective hernia surgery were randomly assigned to low-dose (0.1 mg/kg, n = 35), medium-dose (0.2 mg/kg, n = 36), or high-dose (0.3 mg/kg, n = 35) etomidate groups. All received sufentanil 0.3 μg/kg and remimazolam 0.3 mg/kg with nerve block. Intraoperative vital signs, postoperative cognitive function, and adverse events were compared. Multivariate analysis identified postoperative cognitive dysfunction (POCD) risk factors. RESULTS: The medium-dose group showed superior hemodynamic stability with smaller fluctuations in mean arterial pressure (MAP), systolic blood pressure (SBP), and heart rate (HR), the lowest POCD rate on day 1 (8.3%) and lowest adverse events (13.9%), and shorter recovery and hospital stays. The high-dose group had the highest hypotension (28.6%) and POCD (40.0%) rates. Age ≥75 years, high-dose etomidate, and operative time >60 minutes were independent POCD risk factors. CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: Etomidate 0.2 mg/kg with nerve block achieves favorable hemodynamics and minimizes POCD and adverse reactions in elderly hernia surgery, supporting a moderate-dose strategy for this vulnerable population.
